title: Fixed rules keeps its sort after a rule is added or edited
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA09 cat) exists.
  • Fixed rule part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA09-1) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 30000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA09-2) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 20000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA09-3) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 10000.00).
  • Inventory part {Part-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA09-4) is at {Location-A} in {Category-A} and has no fixed price yet.
  • No other fixed rule at {Location-A} has a fixed price of 10,000 or more.
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Fixed rules tab.
  3. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  4. Click the Fixed Price column header once, so the highest price is first.
  5. Click Add Fixed Rule.
  6. Choose {Part-D}.
  7. Enter the fixed price 25000.00.
  8. Save the dialog.
  9. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  10. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  11. Read the Fixed Price arrow and the first four rows.
  12. Open the fixed rule for {Part-B} for editing.
  13. Change its fixed price to 40000.00.
  14. Save the dialog.
  15. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  16. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  17. Read the Fixed Price arrow and the first four rows.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 11: the Fixed Price arrow still points down and the first four rows read {Part-A} (30,000), {Part-D} (25,000), {Part-B} (20,000), {Part-C} (10,000).
  • Step 17: the arrow still points down and the first four rows read {Part-B} (40,000), {Part-A} (30,000), {Part-D} (25,000), {Part-C} (10,000). The list did not go back to Part Number order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10136 (Story 3, Fixed Rules, sortable columns; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S3-R12a (reload in place, with S3-R8 for the sort used), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas boards 1.4 (Fixed rules - before and after) and 2.1 (The three rules that bite), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Key Decision 'A sort belongs to the user until they leave the page'. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists). The technical plan of 13 Oct 2026 (FR-018, FR-020) says the first click on Fixed price sorts lowest first; PRD version 21 (14 Oct 2026, S3-R4, S3-R8) says highest first and is newer, so this case follows the PRD.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R12a: “When the tab reloads in place, the sort the user chose stays applied and the header arrow stays where it was. Opening the page afresh returns the list to Part number ascending.”
  • S3-R8: “Fixed price sorts by value. Its first click puts the highest price first.”
  • PRD §5 Terminology: “Reload in place - the list refetches while the user stays on the page.”
  • SV-10136 acceptance criteria: “Given a sort is applied, when a fixed rule is created, edited or deleted, then the list reloads with that same sort and arrow still applied.”
